title: Relative right-pinched mapping spaces are Kan fibrations
statement:
Use quasicategories and right-pinched mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. A Kan fibration is a simplicial map lifting every horn of positive dimension, including the outer horns. If $p:E\to B$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories and $x,y\in E$ are vertices, then the induced map
$$\operatorname{Map}_E(x,y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_B(p(x),p(y))$$
is a Kan fibration.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.1 (relative right-pinched mapping-space Kan fibration), printed p.130; read directly in the IAS PDF, saved for this audit in scratch/HTT-second-reading.pdf. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: Put $M=\operatorname{Map}_E(x,y)$ and $N=\operatorname{Map}_B(p(x),p(y))$. Define $q:M\to N$ in degree $n$ by $q_n(\sigma)=p\circ\sigma$. The whole initial face of $p\sigma$ is constant at $p(x)$ and its last vertex is $p(y)$, so this is defined. For each monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, let $\alpha^+:[m+1]\to[n+1]$ extend $\alpha$ by sending the new last vertex to the new last vertex. Then $p(\sigma\alpha^+)=(p\sigma)\alpha^+$. Thus $q$ is precisely the induced simplicial map of the statement, with the operators of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.1, printed p.130: the map on right mapping spaces; explicit postcomposition and operator calculation.

proof.text: We prove that $q$ is a right fibration, meaning that it lifts $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$. Fix such a square with upper map $a:\Lambda_i^n\to M$ and bottom simplex $\beta:\Delta^n\to N$. Regard $\beta$ as a simplex $\bar\beta:\Delta^{n+1}\to B$ with initial face constant at $p(x)$ and last vertex $p(y)$. For every $j\neq i$, $0\leq j\leq n$, the face of $a$ opposite $j$ is a map $\Delta^n\to E$ with initial face constant at $x$ and last vertex $y$; prescribe it on the face $d_j\Delta^n$ of $\Delta^{n+1}$. Prescribe on the remaining face $d_{n+1}\Delta^n$ the constant simplex at $x$. The prescribed coned faces agree on intersections because $a$ is simplicial, and their intersections with $d_{n+1}\Delta^n$ are constant at $x$ by the mapping-space definition. They are exactly the faces of $\Lambda_i^{n+1}$. Their composites with $p$ agree with $\bar\beta$ by commutativity of the original square. Since $0<i<n+1$, [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] supplies an inner-horn lift $\sigma:\Delta^{n+1}\to E$ over $\bar\beta$. Its initial face remains constant at $x$ and its last vertex remains $y$, so $\sigma$ is an $n$-simplex of $M$ giving the required lift of the original square. This is one application of the assumed inner-horn property after identifying its faces, using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. In the smallest case $n=1,i=1$, the two prescribed faces are the initial constant edge and the given edge ending at $y$, and the horn is $\Lambda_1^2$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.1, first two proof sentences; explicit singleton-slice face calculation replacing the invocation of Proposition 2.1.2.1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] with $\mathcal C=B$, $K=\Delta^0$, target vertex $t=p(y)$ and fiber vertex $p(x)$. Its last clause identifies that degreewise slice fiber with the same right-pinched simplicial set $N$ and says it is a Kan complex. The only hypothesis here is that $B$ is a quasicategory, which is assumed; no vertex of $N$, hence no arrow $p(x)\to p(y)$, is required.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.5 and Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX); the Kan-mapping-space input of HTT Lemma 2.4.4.1.

proof.text: Use the first assertion of [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] on $q:M\to N$. Step 2 gives exactly its right-horn lifting range $n\geq1$, $0<i\leq n$, and Step 3 gives its Kan-base hypothesis. All these simplicial sets lie in the fixed sufficiently large universe of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The cited assertion supplies the missing $i=0$ horns as well, so $q$ lifts every positive-dimensional horn. This is the Kan-fibration conclusion in the statement. In particular the proof does not assume that an arbitrary map between Kan complexes is a Kan fibration.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.3.8, implication (3) to (1); equivalently the right-handed version of HTT Lemma 2.1.3.3, the last sentence of the proof of Lemma 2.4.4.1.
